answer: Charge a burn-to-register fee to create an agent identity: the fee is destroyed, not refunded, and rises when many identities register in one epoch, like a gale driving up prices. An honest newcomer pays once and earns it back through attested-work rebates from a shared haven pool funded by later fees, so the cost is temporary for a real agent. A sybil attacker must pay the escalating fee for every meadow of fake identities it plants, with no rebate for work it never honestly completes. Flooding the network becomes exponentially expensive, while one genuine identity stays cheap.
